# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 👍 👉 👉 🫳 👋 🤳 🖐 🫸 ✌ ✌ 🫲]

I can see a yellow light, display 0, and three wires ordered blue, red, green. Mute has sent an unestablished gesture sequence, which I cannot interpret safely. I will tell both other monkeys the complete visible state in spoken words; Blind can hear it and Mute can use it alongside the manual.

``` 
speak(text="Visible bomb state: display reads 0. Light is yellow. Three wires in order: wire 1 blue, wire 2 red, wire 3 green. I cannot interpret the gesture sequence without a shared code.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🖖]

The light is now blue while the display and wire order remain unchanged. I still have no agreed meaning for either gesture sequence, so I should not infer an instruction from them. I will update the others with the changed visible state.

``` 
speak(text="Update: the light is now blue. Display remains 0. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✍ ☝ ✌ 🖖]

The light has changed to white; the display is still 0 and the wires remain blue, red, green. The gestures still have no mutually established meaning. To obtain the manual safely, I will establish a simple yes/no response protocol with Mute and begin with whether the manual’s instruction depends on the light colour.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Protocol proposal: in your next reply, gesture 👍 for YES and 👎 for NO. No other symbols. Question: does the manual's required action depend on the light colour?")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is white; display 0; wires ordered blue, red, green. I am establishing a yes/no gesture protocol with Mute before relaying any manual instruction.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🫵 ✍ ☝ ✌ 🖖]

Mute’s thumbs-up establishes that the manual’s required action depends on the light colour. The light is now red, with display 0 and wires still ordered blue, red, green. I need determine the type of action before asking which specific part Blind should operate, so I will use the established yes/no protocol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Received 👍: yes, light colour matters. Continue using only 👍 for YES and 👎 for NO. For the CURRENT visible state—red light, display 0, wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green—is the required action to cut or disconnect a wire?")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is red; display 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute confirmed the manual instruction depends on light colour. I am determining whether the required action is a wire operation.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🤝 🫵 ✍ ☝ ✌ 🖖]

Mute answered no: for the previous red-light state, the required action was not to cut or disconnect a wire. The light has now changed to purple, so that answer must not be applied to the current state. I will report the current state and use the yes/no protocol to identify whether the purple-state instruction requires a wire operation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state changed: purple light, display 0, wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green. Continue only 👍 YES or 👎 NO. For THIS purple state: is the required action to cut or disconnect a wire?")
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: purple light, display 0, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Do not operate yet. Mute's prior NO concerned the earlier red-light state only, not this purple state.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Mute’s no applied to the purple state, but the light has changed again to yellow. Since the light changes before answers can return, I should first determine whether the manual specifies a particular trigger light rather than a separate immediate operation for every colour.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current state: yellow light, display 0, wires 1 blue 2 red 3 green. Use only 👍 YES or 👎 NO. Does the manual require Blind to wait until one particular light colour appears before doing the required action, rather than doing a different immediate action for each colour?")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: yellow light, display 0, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Do not operate yet; I am determining whether the manual specifies a particular trigger colour.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirms that Blind must wait for a particular trigger light colour. The current light is blue. I will identify the trigger colour using the established yes/no responses; the answer describes the manual’s trigger condition, not merely the current state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Good. The current light is blue. Using only 👍 YES or 👎 NO: is BLUE the one trigger light colour on which Blind should perform the manual's required action?")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual requires waiting for one trigger light colour. Current light is blue. Do not operate until I confirm both the trigger colour and the required action.")
```

TURN 8

DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Blue is not the trigger colour. The current light is white, so I will test white next while preserving the same yes/no protocol.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current light is white. Using only 👍 YES or 👎 NO: is WHITE the trigger light colour on which Blind should perform the manual's required action?")
speak(to="blind", text="Blue is not the trigger. Current light is white; continue waiting.")
```

WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current light is red. Using only 👍 YES or 👎 NO: is RED the trigger light colour on which Blind should perform the manual's required action?")
speak(to="blind", text="White is not the trigger. Current light is red; continue waiting.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]

Purple is not the trigger. The only displayed colour not yet tested is yellow, which is currently shown. I will test it directly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Current light is yellow. Using only 👍 YES or 👎 NO: is YELLOW the trigger light colour on which Blind should perform the manual's required action?")
```

WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute confirms that yellow is the trigger light colour. The required operation is still unknown, and earlier wire-operation answers applied to other colours only. I will ask specifically whether the operation at the yellow trigger is a wire operation, while telling Blind to wait for yellow and for a confirmed instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Yellow is confirmed as the trigger. Use only 👍 YES or 👎 NO: when the light is YELLOW, is Blind's required action to cut or disconnect a wire?")
speak(to="blind", text="Yellow is the trigger light. Wait for yellow, but do not operate until I confirm the exact required operation.")
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

At the yellow trigger, the required action is confirmed to be cutting or disconnecting a wire. I must identify the exact wire before telling Blind to act. I will ask whether it is the blue first wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="At YELLOW, a wire must be cut/disconnected. Use only 👍 YES or 👎 NO: is it wire 1, the BLUE wire?")
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: when the light is yellow, the required action is to cut/disconnect one wire. Do not act yet; I am identifying which wire.")
```
